Handbook: Official MTO Driver's Handbook (Ontario, Canada)
Units: metric (m, km, km/h)
Topic: passing
Batch: the 7 selected passages from the page "Stopping".

[c1] page: Stopping | heading: Stopping for school buses · ¶2 | text
You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.

[c2] page: Stopping | heading: Stopping for school buses · ¶2 | text
If you are coming from behind the bus, stop at least 20 metres away.

[c3] page: Stopping | heading: Stopping for school buses · ¶2 | text
Do not go until the bus moves or the lights have stopped flashing.

[c4] page: Stopping | heading: Stopping for school buses · ¶3 | text
If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop.

[m77] page: Stopping | heading: Stopping for school buses · ¶6 | text
In Ontario, school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus.

[c5] page: Stopping | heading: Stopping for school buses · ¶6 | text
If you don't stop, you can be fined heavily and get six demerit points for a first offence.

[m16] page: Stopping | heading: Stopping for pedestrian crossovers · ¶2 | text
You must not pass any vehicle within 30 metres of a pedestrian crossover.

statements.text: FACT school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have [?illegally passed] a school bus

sources.quote: In Ontario, school bus drivers and other witnesses can report vehicles that have illegally passed a school bus.

flags.note: Implies a prohibition on passing; the law behind it is the duty to stop in 3.4.12b.

statements.note: The law behind it is 3.4.12b, from the same section of the Stopping page.

statements.text: a driver MUST stop WHEN approaching a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, from either direction IF VIOLATED a [?heavy] fine AND 6 demerit points for a first offence

sources.quote: You must stop whenever you approach a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing, regardless of whether you are behind the bus or approaching it from the front.
If you don't stop, you can be fined heavily and get six demerit points for a first offence.

flags.note: The handbook says "fined heavily" and gives no amount.
Repeated on Sharing the road (which also counts the stop arm), the Signs page and the six-point offence table.

statements.note: This duty to stop is what makes passing a stopped school bus illegal (3.4.12a).

statements.text: a driver SHOULD stop at least 20 m from the bus WHEN approaching a stopped school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing from behind

sources.quote: If you are coming from behind the bus, stop at least 20 metres away.

flags.note: A bare imperative right after "You must stop"; it reads as part of the law in 3.4.12b, but the handbook does not say so.

statements.text: a driver SHOULD NOT go WHEN stopped for a school bus with its upper alternating red lights flashing UNTIL the bus moves OR the lights have stopped flashing

sources.quote: Do not go until the bus moves or the lights have stopped flashing.

flags.note: A bare imperative that ends the duty in 3.4.12b; it reads as part of that law, but the handbook does not say so.

flags.span: and its stop arm is no longer activated
flags.note: Elsewhere the stop ends only when every condition holds (bus moves, lights stop, arm folds away); here either one ends it.

statements.text: EXCEPTION TO 3.4.12b WHEN the road has a median strip AND the driver is approaching the bus from the front

sources.quote: If you are on a road with a median strip, only vehicles coming from behind the bus must stop.
